sections.heading: Can: Habilidad en el presente
sections.body: **'Can'** expresa habilidad general en el presente o futuro inmediato (*'I can swim'*). También se utiliza para permisos informales y posibilidad.

sections.heading: Could vs. Was/Were able to: Habilidad en el pasado
sections.body: **'Could'** expresa una habilidad general que se poseía en el pasado (*'I could run fast when I was young'*). Sin embargo, para un **logro específico en una ocasión puntual**, se debe usar **'was/were able to'** o **'managed to'**, no 'could' (*'The firefighters were able to rescue everyone'*).

sections.heading: Be able to: Flexibilidad en todos los tiempos
sections.body: **'Be able to'** no es un verbo modal defectivo, por lo que puede conjugarse en cualquier tiempo verbal (futuro con *will*, presente perfecto con *have been able to*, infinitivo tras otros modales como *might be able to*).

examples.english: She could read when she was four years old.
I was able to finish the marathon despite the heavy rain.
examples.note: Logro específico puntual en el pasado (no 'could finish').

examples.english: You might be able to catch an earlier train.

exercises.instruction: Completa cada oración con la forma correcta de 'can', 'could' o 'be able to'.
items: When I was five, I ___ (can / swim) across the pool.
She ___ (not / can / speak) French when she started the job.
Despite the traffic, we ___ (arrive) on time for the meeting.
Will you ___ (can / help) me with this report tomorrow?

quiz.question: Why is 'could' incorrect in: 'The firefighters ___ rescue everyone from the burning building yesterday'?
options: 'Could' can only refer to future events.
'Could' cannot be used for a specific single achievement in past affirmative sentences; 'were able to' is required.
'Could' cannot be used with plural subjects.
'Could' requires the auxiliary 'have' in all past sentences.
quiz.explanation: For a specific past achievement in a single situation, affirmative sentences require 'was/were able to' or 'managed to', not 'could'.
